# Release v0.6.1

status: DONE

The whole release exists for one defect recorded as the v0.6.0 insight: the version a server
announces in the MCP handshake was a string literal in `src/index.ts`, independent of every
catalogue, and up to five releases stale.

## evidence

### 1. serverInfo.version cannot drift any more

`scripts/sync-versions.mjs` writes `servers/<name>/src/version.ts` from that server's own
`package.json`:

```
// GENERATED by scripts/sync-versions.mjs from this package's package.json. Do not edit.
export const VERSION = "0.6.1";
```

Generation, not a runtime read, because the same sources are vendored into a Cloudflare Workers
bundle where `readFileSync("package.json")` cannot work: there is no filesystem. A generated
source file is the one form both `tsc` and `remote/build-vendor.mjs` compile unchanged.

All 17 `src/index.ts` (16 servers + office-suite) now `import { VERSION } from "./version.js"` and
pass it to `new McpServer(...)`. Four servers already had a hand-maintained `const VERSION`
(calendar, clauses, resume, spreadsheet); those declarations were deleted, the other 13 had a bare
literal. Measured before the change, from `servers/*/src/index.ts`:

```
0.1.0  invoice, price-tracker, spreadsheet, time-tracker, office-suite
0.2.0  expense-tracker
0.3.0  currency, docx, timezone
0.4.0  clauses, recurring, resume
0.5.0  calendar, pdf
0.6.0  bank-statement, image, kanban
```

Hooks: root `package.json` gained `"prebuild": "node scripts/sync-versions.mjs"`, so `npm run
build` regenerates first; `scripts/build-mcpb.sh` calls the same script before it reads any
`package.json`, so a bundle cannot ship a manifest version its binary disagrees with.

`version.ts` was added to all 16 `SERVERS` file lists in `remote/build-vendor.mjs`. It needs no
patching: the vendor pass rewrites its (absent) imports and writes it next to `index.ts`, and the
import specifier `./version.js` is already the repo's own convention.

```
node remote/build-vendor.mjs    16 servers vendored, zero DRIFT
```

One patch did break, and not because of this change: `patch did not apply: expense export
description`. A concurrent agent had reworded `expense_export`'s description in
`servers/expense-tracker/src/index.ts` (commit f15fe98), and the patch matched the old sentence by
exact text. Rewritten to match through the registration instead:

```
/(registerTool\("expense_export",\s*\n\s*title: "[^"]*",\s*\n\s*description: )"[^"]*"/
```

The hosted rewording exists because the export lands in KV as a one-hour download, not on a disk;
that fact is stable, the sentence is not.

Hosted, after `cd remote && wrangler deploy`:

```
POST https://mcp.zovo.one/mcp/kanban   initialize -> serverInfo {"name":"mcp-kanban","version":"0.6.1"}
POST https://mcp.zovo.one/mcp/invoice  initialize -> serverInfo {"name":"mcp-invoice","version":"0.6.1"}
```

Contract test `test/version-contract.test.mjs`, three assertions per server: `src/version.ts`
matches `package.json`, `index.ts` passes `VERSION` rather than a literal, and the live stdio
handshake returns exactly `package.json`'s version. Root `npm test` now runs the workspaces and
then this file. A server directory with a `package.json` but no `src/index.ts` yet skips the two
static checks, so a server another agent is mid-way through creating does not fail the suite.

### 2. KPI reader defects

`data/distribution.json` `per_server.<name>.hosted` holds `"published https://mcp.zovo.one/mcp/x"`.
`scripts/kpi.mjs` tested `s.hosted === "published"`. The URL was appended during the v0.6.0 ledger
rewrite; the equality test then matched nothing and the row read 0 of 16 while all 16 endpoints
were serving. Now a `/^published\b/` prefix test.

"Pro tenants on hosted endpoints" read `remoteKv.by.lic`, a count of KV keys. The keys are
`lic:<key id>:<server>`, one per (key, server) pair: 507 keys, 107 distinct ids, and one validation
run over 16 servers writes 16 of them. The row now counts tenants that money or a person is
attached to:

- `bind:<anon token>` in REMOTE_DATA, written by the billing worker only after Stripe fulfilment;
- `lic:<id>` whose id belongs to a key the billing worker minted. Minted keys live in the LICENSES
  namespace as `session:<checkout session id>`; their payload id is decoded and matched.

Everything else was signed locally by `scripts/sign-license.mjs` from `keys/license-private.pem`,
which is what `scripts/validate.mjs` and `kpi.mjs`'s own latency probe do on every run. The `how`
field names the exclusion with live counts.

`node scripts/kpi.mjs` -> `kpi: 22 indicators, 8 met, 0 unmeasured`. The two rows:

```
Install       Hosted endpoints coverage        16   target 16 of 16 servers   met
              how: data/distribution.json per_server.hosted

Monetization  Pro tenants on hosted endpoints   0   target 20 tenants         zero
              how: Stripe-bound tenants (REMOTE_DATA bind: prefix, 0) plus distinct lic: tenant
              ids whose key the billing worker minted (LICENSES session:*, 0 keys). EXCLUDED: the
              507 raw lic: documents are per (key, server) pairs, not tenants (107 distinct ids),
              and 107 of those ids are validation probes signed locally by
              scripts/sign-license.mjs, never bought.
```

The true value is 0, not 507. LICENSES holds zero `session:*` keys and REMOTE_DATA zero `bind:`
keys, which is the same fact the "License keys minted" and "Paid sessions" rows already report.

### 3. Release

17 packages plus `packages/mcp-license` bumped to 0.6.1, every internal `@theluckystrike/*` range
rewritten to `^0.6.1`, and `server.json` / `server.mcpb.json` / `server.variant.json` versions and
asset URLs with them. `servers/quotes` was excluded throughout: it is another agent's server and
its owner releases it. Its `^0.6.0` range on `mcp-license` still resolves to 0.6.1.

```
npm install        ok
npm run build      18 workspaces, tsc clean
npm test           tests 710, pass 695, fail 0, skipped 11
bash scripts/build-mcpb.sh   exit 0, 17 bundles, manifests at 0.6.1
```

Push before the release, per the v0.6.0 failure: `ed35e83..ef09158 main -> main`, then
`gh release create v0.6.1 bundles/*.mcpb` -> 17 assets at
https://github.com/theluckystrike/mcp-servers/releases/tag/v0.6.1.

sha256 of each bundle written into its `server.mcpb.json` and `server.variant.json` `fileSha256`,
with the v0.6.1 asset URL as identifier. kanban:
`2575e076e2b6bcd80e66164097e5951a81e3c9ca89361e0e9a77682020080443`.

`mcp-publisher login github -token "$(gh auth token)"` once, then 17 `server.mcpb.json` and 13
`server.variant.json` published, no 422s (the 100-char description limit that bit v0.6.0 was
already fixed in those files). Verified by exact-name lookup through
`GET /v0/servers?search=<short name>&version=latest`: **30 of 30 at 0.6.1**. The unqualified
`search=theluckystrike` listing still returns a deprecated `io.github.theluckystrike/invoice` at
0.1.1, which is not one of the 30 and is filtered by status in `kpi.mjs`.

`scripts/sync-mirrors.sh` exit 0, 17 repos pushed.

`data/distribution.json`: 49 version fields moved from 0.6.0 to 0.6.1 across `per_server` and the
`surfaces` notes.

## cost

38 wall minutes. Zero paid API calls.

## failures

1. `remote/build-vendor.mjs` threw `patch did not apply: expense export description` after a
   concurrent agent reworded that tool. Fixed by anchoring the patch on
   `registerTool("expense_export", ...)` instead of the description text.
2. `git -c rebase.autoStash=true pull --rebase` failed to reapply its own autostash
   (`could not reset --hard / Aborting`) and left the repo mid-rebase with the replay already
   done. The working tree was diffed against the stash commit first (identical for every tracked
   path), then `git rebase --quit` cleared the state without touching HEAD or the tree, and the
   stash was dropped after the commit landed.

## insight

The generated-file fix is worth more than the version numbers it corrects: `src/version.ts` is the
only shape that survives both build targets. A runtime `readFileSync("package.json")` is the
obvious fix and is impossible here, because the same TypeScript is vendored into a Workers bundle
with no filesystem; a build-time `define`/env substitution works for the worker and not for
`npx`-installed stdio. Measured cost of the drift it removes: at v0.6.0 every outward surface
(bundle manifest, registry entry, package.json, mirror) said 0.6.0 while 14 of 17 handshakes said
something older, four of them 0.1.0. The same class of defect produced this release's KPI bug:
`s.hosted === "published"` was true when written and silently false once a URL was appended to the
value, reporting 0 of 16 live endpoints for as long as anyone was reading the dashboard. Both are
one writer and one reader agreeing on a literal, with nothing asserting they still agree. The
contract test is the part that does not drift.
